Reference windows for survey summaries

Source: R/windows.R
window_lag.Rd

Describe the period before each interview over which summarise_by_interview() summarises the indicators.

Usage

window_lag(interval = "1 year", n_lags = 0)

window_season(start_month, end_month, years_back = 0)

window_fixed(from, to)

window_since(event)

Arguments

interval

Length of each lag, e.g. "1 year", "6 months", "30 days".

n_lags

Highest lag; 0 gives only the period just before the interview.

start_month, end_month

Season bounds: numbers, abbreviations or month names.

years_back

Which past seasons: 0 is the last one, 0:2 the last three.

from, to

Dates of a fixed window, inclusive.

event

<data-masking> Column of the survey with the start date of each household's window.

Value

A c4e_window object.

Details

  • window_lag(): consecutive periods of interval before the interview, e.g. the 12 months before it (lag 0) and the 12 months before those (lag 1). The interview day itself is never included.

  • window_season(): the last season that ended before the interview, and earlier ones with years_back, e.g. the June to September rains. A season may cross the new year ("Nov" to "Feb").

  • window_fixed(): the same calendar period for everyone.

  • window_since(): from a date recorded for each household, such as planting or a shock, up to the day before the interview.

See also

summarise_by_interview()

Examples

window_lag("1 year", n_lags = 2)
#> <c4e window: 1 year before the interview, lags 0 to 2>
window_season("Jun", "Sep", years_back = 0:1)
#> <c4e window: season Jun to Sep, 0, 1 season(s) back>
window_fixed("2022-01-01", "2022-12-31")
#> <c4e window: from 2022-01-01 to 2022-12-31>
